articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric obesity is a major public health crisis. Early identification of metabolic traits that increase individual risk are emerging. As such, identification of variability in early energy expenditure would reveal the need for precision nutritional approaches from birth. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the interindividual variability in components of energy expenditure for the purpose of understanding early nutritional considerations in very young infants. METHODS: Infant participants (<3 months of age) underwent extensive energy expenditure phenotyping using a combination of doubly labeled water for total daily energy expenditure and a novel infant metabolic chamber for sleeping energy expenditure. Descriptive statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients, and univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses were used to assess reliability and characterize variability, predictors, and phenotypes of energy expenditure. We identified interindividual variability in total, mass-adjusted, and fat-free mass adjusted energy expenditures. Energy phenotypes (thrifty and spendthrift) were assigned based on the residuals between measured and predicted energy expenditure from metabolic mass. Discrepancies between measured energy expenditure and predicted by national dietary recommendations for infants (2023 DRI) were evaluated. RESULTS: Total daily and sleeping energy expenditures were 368±60 kcal/d and 250±60 kcal/d, respectively. Energy expenditure related to activity accounted for 21±9% of total measured. Age (r=.59), weight (r=.83), length (r=.75), and fat-free mass (r=.82) were positively associated with sleeping energy expenditure. We identified 40% of measured infants with a thrifty energy phenotype, classified as having sleeping energy expenditure under that predicted by cohort age, sex, and fat and fat-free mass. Mean prediction error of the 2023 DRI from our cohort was 10±7% and was positively associated with the amount of energy expenditure attributed to activity. CONCLUSIONS: These findings warrant further comprehensive metabolic phenotyping studies in young infants to understand how early energy expenditure tracks through the life course and influences obesity risk as well as the thorough evaluation and refinement of infant nutritional recommendations.

articles.title: Large Language Models and Applied Surgical Anatomy: Evaluation of Anatomical Reasoning in Expert-Derived Plastic Surgery Scenarios.
articles.authors: Menekşe Kastamoni Başkan, Süleyman Çeçen, Yadigar Kastamoni
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into medical education, research, and clinical decision-support applications; however, their ability to apply anatomical knowledge in clinically relevant surgical scenarios remains insufficiently studied. This study evaluated and compared the performance of six contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, Copilot, and Manus) using 25 expert-derived applied surgical anatomy scenarios relevant to plastic surgery. Scenarios were developed by an expert panel consisting of one associate professor of anatomy and two plastic surgeons. Responses were generated using a standardized prompt and assessed with a structured scoring rubric evaluating anatomical accuracy, clinical reasoning, completeness, and safety, with a maximum score of 10 points per question. Critical errors were additionally assessed. Significant differences in overall performance were observed among models (Friedman χ2 = 43.51, p < 0.001). ChatGPT achieved the maximum aggregate score (250/250), followed by Gemini (248/250), DeepSeek (241/250), Copilot (240/250), Claude (235/250), and Manus (219/250). Critical errors were infrequent and were confined to a reconstructive vascular physiology scenario: DeepSeek, Claude, and Manus each demonstrated one observed critical error, whereas ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot demonstrated none. Although all evaluated models demonstrated excellent performance, clinically significant anatomical misconceptions persisted despite high aggregate scores. These findings demonstrate strong performance by the tested LLMs on this specific scenario-based benchmark, while also identifying clinically meaningful anatomical errors in a subset of responses. Future evaluations should focus not only on overall accuracy but also on clinically meaningful error patterns that may influence surgical decision-making. Importantly, substantial ceiling effects limited discrimination among high-performing models, and the findings should therefore be interpreted as performance on this specific benchmark rather than as evidence of a general hierarchy of anatomical reasoning capability.

articles.title: One Carbon Metabolism - The Missing Link for Cancer and Sepsis.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Abigail Anderson, Carter Weeg
articles.abstract: One-carbon (1C) metabolism (OCM) is a biosynthetic and physiological process essential to cells. OCM encompasses a multitude of tightly regulated biochemical reactions that are responsible for nucleotide synthesis (purines and pyrimidines), amino acid homeostasis (Met, Ser, Gly), redox balance, and epigenetic regulation. Dysregulations of this pathway have been implicated in the development and progression of cancer and sepsis - two complex pathologies, each with a characteristically high morbidity and mortality rate. OCM changes in the oncogenic state have been extensively investigated, while metabolic pathway changes in sepsis remain more elusive. Given that emerging evidence suggests that 1 in 5 sepsis hospitalizations occur in patients with a cancer diagnosis, and recovering sepsis patients have a higher incidence of cancer diagnosis, our review aims to analyze the known OCM changes that occur in each pathology, highlight commonalities and variations, and suggest clinical implications that explore possible therapeutic targets. Through a novel cross-disease examination, a more comprehensive understanding of OCM metabolic changes in these disease states could inform clinical practice and lead to the development of targeted therapeutic interventions that further our understanding and treatment of one or both conditions.

articles.title: Longitudinal Analysis of Skeletal Muscle and Cardiometabolic Risk During the Menopause Transition.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Hannah E Cabre, Kaja Falkenhain, Steve R Smith et al.
articles.abstract: We assessed longitudinal changes in body composition and cardiometabolic risk in those with normal-weight and overweight/obese women across the menopausal transition. We examined a 10-year longitudinal analysis of 81 healthy women in the prospective Healthy Transitions cohort. Body composition measures were obtained via dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Skeletal muscle was estimated using a validated prediction model: 1.12 × appendicular lean mass- 0.63. Serum sex steroid hormones and cardiometabolic factors were quantified in fasting blood. Participants were stratified by BMI into normal weight (n=41) and overweight/obesity (n=40) groups. Changes within and between BMI groups across the menopause transition were assessed with linear mixed models. At menopause onset, compared to those with normal weight, participants with overweight/obesity had lower sex hormone-binding globulin (-30.9±10.3 nmol/L; p=0.01), greater percent body fat (13.1±1.3%; p<0.001), greater skeletal muscle mass (2.5±0.6 kg; p<0.001), and worse cardiometabolic risk factors (p<0.001). In the 5 years before menopause, participants with overweight/obesity gained skeletal muscle (+1.2 kg) and fat mass (+3.5 kg), while participants with normal weight increased percent body fat (+1.5%) only. At menopause onset, women with overweight/obesity exhibit distinct alterations in body composition, hormonal profiles, and cardiometabolic risk that exist in the years preceding menopause, highlighting the importance of early, targeted interventions to mitigate adverse health trajectories during the menopause transition.

articles.title: Cardiovascular dietary guidance at an inflection point: the 2025-2030 US dietary guidelines versus the 2026 AHA scientific statement.
articles.authors: Luiz Fernando Sella, Daniela Kanno

articles.title: The impact of work-related foot pain on work and personal life: an interview study.
articles.authors: Ann-Sophie Hörnell, Anncristine Fjellman-Wiklund, Åsa Svedmark et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The occurrence of foot pain is high, especially in those with physically demanding occupations. Work-related foot pain has been shown to impact work performance, family life, and leisure activities. While prevalence across various sectors is documented, research exploring experiences and total life impact of work-related foot pain remains limited. AIM: The aim of this study was to explore experiences of living with foot pain among individuals employed in highly demanding physical occupations, and occupations characterised by prolonged standing or walking. METHODS: A qualitative, semi-structured interview-based approach was chosen. Twelve individual interviews were conducted with nine women and three men, and analysed using Qualitative Content Analysis. RESULTS: One main theme, Walking a fine line - Balancing challenges in multiple aspects of life due to work-related foot pain, and three sub-themes were identified, describing how external work-environment factors and internal experiences of autonomy impact an individual's overall life situation, including impact on family life and the mental toll of living and working with foot pain. The sub-theme Struggling with increased pain due to work conditions and environment highlights how factors such as certain types of floors, physical work demands, time spent on the feet, walking, heavy lifting, and inadequate footwear directly exacerbate pain. The sub-theme Feeling like just another cog in the machine due to limited control over workplace organisation reflects difficulties for employees in influencing work tasks, planning daily work tasks and responsibilities, a lack of recovery during the workday, and communication within the workplace. The sub-theme Experiencing inequality and low quality of life outside of work describes the consequences for individuals' personal lives, including restricted social participation, strained family relations, negative emotions, and sleep disturbances. Overall, the individuals expressed a sense of resignation, feeling that they had to "grit their teeth" and continue working despite the pain. CONCLUSION: The central findings of this study are negative experiences and struggles, during both work and leisure time. Understanding the experiences of individuals with work-related foot pain can help employers and healthcare providers to identify work-related risks and consider preventative measures, although further research on this topic is needed. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Dynamical systems-based metrics reveal fatigue-related biomechanical changes during running in endurance-trained male and female runners.
articles.authors: Yiyang Chen, Jill Emmerzaal, Gleydciane A Fernandes et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Linear and nonlinear metrics derived from a small number of accelerometers provide global insight into fatigue-related changes and injury risk. RESEARCH QUESTION: This study aimed to determine the effects of fatigue on movement dynamics estimated from lower-back accelerometry between endurance-trained male and female runners. METHODS: Thirty-two endurance-trained runners (16 females) performed a fatiguing running task until volitional exhaustion (20 on the Borg CR20 scale), while wearing one inertial measurement unit (IMU) placed on their pelvis/lower back. Step and stride regularity (unbiased autocorrelation), root mean square (RMS)-based measures of variability (absolute RMS and RMS ratio), complexity (Sample Entropy), jerk-based measure of smoothness (Log Dimensionless Jerk; LDLJ), and stability (short- and long-term Lyapunov Exponent) were calculated from the raw accelerations. RESULTS: Significant main effects of fatigue were observed across both sexes for gait regularity, with an 8% reduction in anteroposterior step regularity and an 11% reduction in stride regularity. Fatigue also altered variability characteristics, resulting in a 12% increase in mediolateral absolute RMS, a 13% increase in anteroposterior absolute RMS, a 2% decrease in vertical RMS ratio, a 6% increase in mediolateral RMS ratio, and an 8% increase in anteroposterior RMS ratio. Fatigue increased movement complexity, as evidenced by a 14% increase in vertical Sample Entropy and an 11% increase in anteroposterior Sample Entropy. In addition to these overall fatigue effects, RMS-based measure of variability showed sex-specific responses. Interaction effects showed that males exhibited a 4% increase in the vertical absolute RMS of lower-back acceleration with fatigue, whereas females did not. SIGNIFICANCE: Both male and female endurance-trained runners may adopt a less regular and less predictable whole-body movement pattern with fatigue, while RMS-based variability showed sex-specific responses, with increased fatigue-related changes in males. These findings highlight the importance of considering both general and sex-specific adaptations when monitoring fatigue.

articles.title: Individual Calibration of a Multiinput Wearable Device Improves Exercise Energy Expenditure Estimation During Intermittent High-Intensity but Not Resistance Exercise in an Athletic Female Population.
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Rebekka Frazer, Christopher D Askew, Amy-Lee Bowler et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to determine the accuracy of a multiinput wearable device (Actiheart 5) and commercially available accelerometer (GENEActiv) in the estimation of exercise energy expenditure (EEE) during intermittent high-intensity and resistance exercise sessions among 31 trained females. Data were collected over two testing sessions involving (a) measurement of resting metabolic rate, physique and a graded exercise test on a treadmill to enable individualized calibration of the wearables, and (b) A modified Bath University Rugby Union Shuttle Test followed by a resistance exercise session. GENEActiv and Actiheart EEE-derived measures, using both generic and individually calibrated algorithms, were compared against (a) indirect calorimetry for Bath University Rugby Union Shuttle Test and (b) indirect calorimetry plus the estimated anaerobic energy contribution based on blood lactate responses for resistance exercise. Equivalence was evaluated using predefined bounds of ±10% mean indirect calorimetry EEE. The use of individually-calibrated Actiheart algorithms improved estimation of EEE during Bath University Rugby Union Shuttle Test (mean bias 4.5 ± 60.4 kcal) compared with individually-calibrated GENEActiv algorithms (mean bias 69.5 ± 86.6 kcal), and equivalence with indirect calorimetry was achieved, although substantial individual error remained (95% limits of agreement -113.9 to 122.8 kcal and intraclass correlation coefficients, .62 [.34 to .80]). Individualized Actiheart algorithms provided equivalent group-level estimates of EEE during intermittent high-intensity exercise, whereas neither Actiheart nor GENEActiv demonstrated acceptable validity or equivalence against the reference method for resistance training, suggesting Metabolic Equivalents of Task may be a more practical method of estimating EEE.

articles.title: General Morphology and Neurite Projection Patterns of Supramedullary Neurons in the Cunner, Tautogolabrus adspersus.
articles.authors: Nick Hiza, Jun Liu, Tina Wong et al.
articles.abstract: Supramedullary neurons (SMNs) are located on the dorsal surface of the hindbrain and spinal cord in many adults of teleost fishes. Comparative morphological studies have revealed differences in SMN size, number and distribution among fishes. However, little information exists on the projection patterns of SMN neurites within the central nervous system. We focus on a single species of adult teleost fish, the cunner, Tautogolabrus adspersus, a fish that has 25-46 SMN somata aligned dorsally along the midline in the hindbrain and rostral third of the spinal cord. Light and transmission electron microscopic techniques provide new information on the general morphology of SMNs and Lucifer yellow filled SMNs reveal that these neurons are not morphologically homogeneous. Rather, four different morphotypes can be identified based on projection patterns of major neurites in the hindbrain and spinal cord wholemounts. The morphological variations suggest that some SMNs exit the brain exclusively through the first dorsal root while others exit the central nervous system through a dorsal root and the trigeminal nerve. Despite the remarkable size and accessibility of SMNs, their function(s) remains unknown. One proposed role of these cells is eliciting mucous secretion in response to skin abrasion from predation. Variation in projection patterns in the cunner provides a morphological framework from which to design electrophysiological studies to help reveal SMN function.

articles.title: Reduced spike adaptation in RHEB/mTORC1-hyperactive excitatory neurons influences network hyperactivity.
articles.authors: Anouk M Heuvelmans, Stefan G J Lip, Mario Negrello et al.
articles.abstract: The mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) pathway plays a crucial role in structural brain development by regulating cell growth, metabolism and other cellular processes. Hyperactivation of this pathway causes refractory epilepsy and enhanced network activity through increased synaptic connectivity. However, patch-clamp recordings of neurons in which the mTOR pathway is hyperactive revealed reduced intrinsic excitability. To unravel the mechanism underlying this paradoxical finding, we combine whole-cell recordings from dissociated murine hippocampal neurons overexpressing the gain-of-function Ras-homolog enriched in brain (RHEB)-p.P37L mutation, with an in silico model to connect cellular changes to network dynamics. We found an increased rheobase, decreased depolarization-induced excitability and increased afterhyperpolarization current in mTORC1-hyperactive neurons, confirming hypo-excitability. Further characterization of spike-trains revealed a lack of adaptation in these neurons, enabling neurons to reach shorter interspike intervals in response to higher current injections. We built a computational model of the neurons that reproduces the electrophysiological parameters we measured. This model revealed the interaction between the afterhyperpolarization current and voltage-dependent refractory mechanisms as a potential cause for the reduction in spike adaptation. Network simulation revealed how passive properties, afterhyperpolarization current, and synaptic connectivity contribute to aberrant network activity, suggesting the altered passive properties in RHEB-p.P37L neurons as a cause of reduced burst rhythmicity on network level. Our findings indicate that, in mTORC1-hyperactive neurons, excitability is regulated in a state-dependent manner, where baseline hypo-excitability coexists with poor adaptation, promoting high-frequency firing in high-input states. Based on our results, we propose that, in addition to altered synaptic connectivity, differences in state-dependent neuronal excitability underlie mTOR-hyperactivity-induced disruptions of network activity. KEY POINTS: The mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) pathway is essential for brain development, and hyperactivation of the pathway causes refractory epilepsy and increased neuronal network activity. Neurons with induced mTORC1-hyperactivity display intrinsic hypo-excitability at the single-cell level but exhibit stronger synaptic connectivity in networks than controls. Single-cell recordings from murine primary hippocampal neurons expressing the gain-of-function Ras-homolog enriched in brain (RHEB)-p.P37L mutation reveal increased afterhyperpolarization currents and a marked reduction in spike-frequency adaptation, allowing neurons to fire at shorter interspike intervals during strong current injection. A biophysically constrained computational neuron model recapitulating the biological single-cell intrinsic properties reproduced faster firing in response to strong current injection, and revealed how passive properties, afterhyperpolarization and synaptic connectivity contribute to aberrant network activity. The findings demonstrate state-dependent regulation of excitability in mTORC1-hyperactive neurons, where baseline hypo-excitability coexists with impaired adaptation and high-frequency firing, suggesting that altered intrinsic excitability, in addition to increased synaptic connectivity, contributes to mTOR-driven network dysfunction.

articles.title: Revisiting the ontogenetic status of the Late Pleistocene human frontal bone from Klasies River Main Site.
articles.authors: Frederick E Grine, Timothy G Bromage, Anton du Plessis et al.
articles.abstract: The ontogenetic status of the Middle Stone Age human frontal bone (SAM-AP 6301) from Klasies River Mouth Main Site is relevant to the interpretation of this fossil's morphology. Some maintain that it represents a modern adult, while others argue that it may be from an archaic juvenile, which could explain its lack of a pronounced supraorbital torus. We employed μCT imaging to investigate the nasofrontal suture and frontal sinus, which were used in previous age assessments. High-resolution replicas of the brow region were examined to document its surface micromorphology with respect to vermiculate pattern development. The nasofrontal suture shows little evidence of fusion either internally or ectocranially, but this only indicates that the specimen is unlikely to have been from an aged adult. The frontal sinus is comparatively small, but its volume can be easily matched among other Late Pleistocene human fossils and recent indigenous populations of southern Africa. The anterior and posterior sinus walls are formed by compact bone, whereas its roof is intermittently porous, possibly reflecting active resorption-pneumatic expansion into the frontal squama-at time of death. This may suggest subadult development, although continued sinus expansion into adulthood cannot be ruled out. The surface of the brow region exhibits at most a slight to moderate vermiculate development, but this also may not necessarily be indicative of age. While the patency of the frontonasal suture and the apparently resorptive nature of the frontal sinus roof seem to be more commensurate with adolescence, the ontogenetic age of the Klasies frontal remains unresolved.

articles.title: Joint associations of EAT-Lancet diet adherence and ambient air-pollution mixtures with respiratory disease risk: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Yemei Chen, Chuanchuan Yu, Liying Zhao et al.
articles.abstract: Whether sustainable dietary patterns and real-world multipollutant exposure are jointly associated with respiratory disease risk remains unclear. We prospectively analysed 64,212 UK Biobank participants with assessment-centre Oxford WebQ data as the primary dietary analysis cohort, with additional analyses incorporating participants with at least one or at least two valid dietary assessments. Adherence to the EAT-Lancet diet was derived from 24-h dietary recall data. For each outcome, an air-pollution mixture score (APS) integrating PM2.5, PM10, PMcoarse, NO2 and NOx was constructed by applying weights estimated from covariate-adjusted weighted quantile sum regression in the corresponding eligible UK Biobank pollution cohort to the dietary analysis cohorts. Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations with incident overall respiratory disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma. Each 1-SD higher APS was associated with higher risks of overall respiratory disease (hazard ratio [HR] 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.10) and COPD (HR 1.09, 95% CI 1.04-1.15), but not asthma. Each 1-point higher EAT-Lancet score was associated with lower risks of overall respiratory disease (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97-0.98) and COPD (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.97), but not asthma. Compared with participants with low EAT-Lancet adherence and high APS, those with high adherence and low APS had lower risks of overall respiratory disease (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.66-0.82), COPD (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.54-0.74), and asthma (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68-0.95). Formal interaction tests were not statistically significant in the primary analysis, although COPD interaction estimates were consistently positive across dietary analyses, with the strongest evidence among participants with at least one valid dietary assessment (RERI 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.37). Higher EAT-Lancet adherence and lower multipollutant exposure were jointly associated with lower respiratory disease risks, particularly COPD, suggesting that sustainable dietary patterns may complement population-level air-quality policies.

articles.title: Multisite Implementation and Outcomes of KineTransForma: A Faculty-Supervised, Student-Delivered, Community-Based, Goal-Directed Home Rehabilitation Program in Chile.
articles.authors: Paul Medina-González, Pablo Morales-Barrientos, Hugo Tapia-Gallardo et al.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Home-based rehabilitation for functional dependency is difficult to deliver at scale in settings where timely access to physical therapy is constrained. Pragmatic evidence is needed on feasible models that make implementation and outcomes visible under real-world conditions. OBJECTIVE: The objective was to evaluate the implementation and outcomes of KineTransForma, a faculty-supervised, student-delivered, community-based, goal-directed home rehabilitation program in Chile. DESIGN: This multisite pragmatic program evaluation used a nonrandomized pre-post design and was guided by the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance framework. SETTING: The evaluation was conducted at 3 community sites in a south-central Chilean region during the 2025 program cycle. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 42 dependency contexts were included, each defined as an adult with functional dependency or risk of dependency and the immediate in-home care network. Patients had a mean age of 65.29 years; 31 of 42 were female, and a primary caregiver was identified in 38 of 42 contexts. INTERVENTION(S) OR EXPOSURE(S): Supervised home sessions were delivered by physical therapy students under faculty supervision across semester-based fieldwork periods. Progression was anchored to the Critical Functional Context-Maximum Motor Milestone (CFC-MaxMM) and a therapeutic-window framework integrating task performance, physiological cost, and perceived exertion. MAIN OUTCOME(S) AND MEASURE(S): Implementation indicators included delivered sessions, total minutes, and caregiver involvement. Effectiveness outcomes were Barthel Index, Elderly Mobility Scale , manual muscle testing-derived global strength, and CFC-MaxMM distribution. RESULTS: Mean program exposure was 17.45 sessions and 1618.93 minutes per context. A formal caregiver was identified in 90.5% of contexts. Barthel Index, Elderly Mobility Scale, and global strength increased from baseline to postintervention, and CFC-MaxMM distribution shifted toward higher mobility levels. CONCLUSIONS: KineTransForma was feasibly implemented across 3 community sites and yielded favorable functional signals under routine-care constraints. RELEVANCE: These findings support the relevance of a pragmatic, milestone-anchored home rehabilitation model while justifying further study with stronger designs and follow-up.

articles.title: A reexamination of the extinct batoid genus Protoplatyrhina, with notes on the evolutionary relationships of Cretaceous rhinopristiforms.
articles.authors: Benjamin Spencer Goode
articles.abstract: The Late Cretaceous batoid Protoplatyrhina has been the subject to contestation regarding its phylogenetic positioning. Reassessment of the holotype and referred specimens of the Late Cretaceous rhinopristiform Protoplatyrhina hopii Williamson et al., 1993 reveals that the diagnostic dental characteristic described for the species, the lack of a lingual crown uvula, is not consistent with some referred specimens. The presence of a uvula appears to be variable within Protoplatyrhina hopii; when present, the uvula is less pronounced than typical of most teeth from Protoplatyrhina renae Case, 1978. Protoplatyrhina bourdoni sp. nov. is erected for teeth from the Hosta Tongue of the Point Lookout Sandstone in New Mexico, USA. Prior attributions to Protoplatyrhina renae are assessed, with the present work finding that multiple purported occurrences likely belong to additional undescribed taxa, indicating overlooked intrageneric diversity. Protoplatyrhinidae fam. nov. is erected to classify Protoplatyrhina, Angolabatis, an undescribed taxon from the Lower Barremian of Spain, and possibly Pseudohypolophus. Hypsobatidae is herein restricted to Hypsobatis and Youssoubatis on the basis of possessing the plesiomorphic characteristic of a distinct transverse keel on the occlusal surface of the crown. Conversely, the stratigraphically older members of Protoplatyrhinidae fam. nov. typically do not feature a transverse keel, with only members of the genus Protoplatyrhina possessing it, albeit uncommonly, more weakly when present, and on teeth of "wide" or "median-width" morphology, possibly as an atavistic expression.

articles.title: Association between maternal food addiction and anaemia among mothers and their children living in socially vulnerable situations.
articles.authors: Luiz Gonzaga Ribeiro Silva-Neto, Risia Cristina Egito de Menezes, Thays Lane Ferreira Dos Santos et al.
articles.abstract: The objective of this study was to evaluate the association between food addiction (FA) and the presence of anaemia in mother-child pairs living in socially vulnerable situations. This population-based cross-sectional study was conducted in urban slums and communities in Maceió, Alagoas, Brazil, between 2020 and 2021. A total of 401 mother-child dyads (children aged 6-59 months) were evaluated. Children of both sexes were included. FA was identified using the mYFAS 2·0 questionnaire, validated for Portuguese. Anaemia was determined based on Hb concentration. Poisson regression models with robust variance estimates were used, adjusted for socio-demographic variables, nutritional status and lifestyle factors. The prevalence of maternal FA was 21·4 %, whereas anaemia was observed in 64·8 % of mothers and 50·1 % of children. The presence of maternal FA was associated with a 41 % higher prevalence of anaemia among women (prevalence ratio = 1·41; 95 % CI: 1·05, 1·89; p = 0·020) and a 25 % higher prevalence of anaemia among their children (prevalence ratio = 1·25; 95 % CI: 1·08, 1·46; p = 0·003). These findings highlight the potential relevance of behavioural factors related to eating in the context of anaemia among mothers and children living in socially vulnerable situations. Further longitudinal studies are needed to investigate the temporal relationship between maternal FA and anaemia in mothers and their children.

articles.title: Cellular composition and morphology of the human nasal epithelium in the superior turbinate.
articles.authors: Daiana Yedgey, Victoria F Low, Maurice A Curtis
articles.abstract: The sense of smell is essential for environmental awareness, food safety, and quality of life, yet it is vulnerable to aging, environmental insults, viruses, and neurological disease. Our understanding of the cellular composition and morphology of the human nasal epithelium is heavily influenced by rodent studies or small biopsies from humans. The human nasal cavity contains three epithelial types: olfactory epithelium (OE), transitional epithelium (TE), and respiratory epithelium (RE). Epithelial types differ in the relative composition of olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) and supporting cells. However, the intact human nasal mucosa has not been studied in detail. Here, we characterized the morphology of tissue from large en bloc specimens (>7 cm3) that included both cranial and facial aspects of the olfactory system of 13 embalmed human cadavers. Using histochemical stains, chromogenic and fluorescent immunohistochemistry with markers targeting cilia, sustentacular cells, basal cells, olfactory neurons, olfactory ensheathing cells, fibroblasts, and cell membranes, we assessed the epithelial morphology and continuity from OE through TE to RE. A custom image-analysis pipeline was developed to quantify epithelial thickness and delineate the epithelial subtypes. Our findings demonstrate distinct cellular compositions and structural organization across OE, TE, and RE, confirm variable OE thickness compared with RE, and highlight complex epithelial transitions not captured in small biopsies. This work provides an integrated anatomical and molecular characterization of the human nasal epithelium across its full anatomical extent, establishing a foundational reference for the study of aging, disease, and olfactory dysfunction.

articles.title: Correction to: Reporting Completeness of Systematic Reviews of Nutrition or Diet-Related Randomised Controlled Trials: A Meta-Research on Adherence to PRISMA Items.
DEL-1 deficiency exacerbates inflammation-driven cardiac dysfunction during angiotensin II-induced hypertension.
articles.authors: Alina Maslakova, Maria Knyrim, Michael Marterstock et al.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is associated with inflammatory activation in the heart that contributes to cardiac remodelling and functional impairment, yet the mechanisms that regulate these cardiac inflammatory responses remain incompletely understood. Developmental endothelial locus-1 (DEL-1) is a secreted immunomodulatory glycoprotein that regulates leukocyte recruitment and inflammation resolution; however, its constitutive role in cardiac inflammation and remodelling during hypertension has not been defined. Here, we investigated the function of DEL-1 during angiotensin II (ANGII)-induced hypertension using Del1-deficient mice. Echocardiographic analysis revealed a distinct temporal pattern of cardiac remodelling during ANGII infusion. Del1KO mice developed early systolic dysfunction accompanied by diastolic alterations three days after ANGII infusion, whereas wild-type (WT) littermates maintained preserved systolic performance at this stage. Importantly, these functional differences occurred in the absence of differences in arterial pressure, suggesting a blood pressure independent mechanism. Flow cytometric analysis demonstrated markedly enhanced recruitment of neutrophils and inflammatory Ly6Chi monocytes into Del1KO hearts during the early phase of hypertension, indicating amplified inflammatory activation. This was accompanied by activation of the bone marrow haematopoietic compartment, characterized by an early expansion of long-term haematopoietic stem cells, followed by a transient increase in haematopoietic progenitor populations during the intermediate phase of hypertension. During later stages of hypertension, systolic function partially recovered in Del1KO mice but was accompanied by exaggerated hypertrophic remodelling and increased cardiac fibrosis. Together, these findings identify DEL-1 as an endogenous regulator that restrains early cardiac inflammation at the onset of hypertension and supports balanced cardiac adaptation during prolonged hypertensive stress. KEY POINTS: Hypertension is associated with cardiac inflammation and remodelling, but endogenous mechanisms that restrain early inflammatory cardiac injury remain incompletely defined. Developmental endothelial locus-1 (DEL-1) deficiency caused early systolic dysfunction and diastolic alterations during angiotensin II-induced hypertension, despite no early difference in arterial blood pressure. Loss of DEL-1 amplified early recruitment of neutrophils and Ly6Chi inflammatory monocytes to the heart and was associated with activation of the bone marrow haematopoietic compartment. At later stages, systolic function partially recovered in Del1KO mice, but this was accompanied by exaggerated fibrotic remodelling and increased profibrotic gene expression. These findings identify endogenous DEL-1 as a protective regulator that limits early inflammatory cardiac injury and supports balanced cardiac adaptation during hypertensive stress.

articles.title: The Development of the Strength and Conditioning Coach Evaluation Tool.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: David LaPlaca, Paul Schempp, Jeremy Elliott et al.
articles.abstract: LaPlaca, D, Schempp, P, Elliott, J, Weldon, A, and Bishop, C. The development of the strength and conditioning coach evaluation tool. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to develop a tool to assess the level of coaching skills of strength and conditioning (S&C) coaches. The study involved 213 S&C coaches working on the elite level with an average of 13.8 years of experience, employed across Major League Baseball, Major League Soccer, National Basketball Association, National Football League, National Hockey League, Armed Forces, Australian Football League, English Premier League, and NCAA Division 1 FBS "Power Five" Conferences. Subjects completed an evaluation form composed of qualitative and quantitative questions. Hereafter, 22 subjects further completed a test-retest within 2 weeks, the intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.771 (95% confidence interval: 0729-0.807), demonstrating statistical reliability. This study has produced a preliminary evaluation tool that is reliable for evaluating S&C coaching expertise. It can be used by S&C coaches, their supervisors, and non-S&C managers to guide professional development and assesses the current skills, knowledge, and experiences of a S&C coach.

articles.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence or Telerehabilitation on Consumer Ratings in Physical Therapy: An Online Randomized Experiment.
articles.authors: Megan H Ross, Joshua Simmich, Daniela Berg et al.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into health care delivery, but its influence on consumer perceptions of physical therapist services remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: The objective was to examine how the use of AI influences consumer perceptions of in-person and telerehabilitation physical therapist services. DESIGN: This study used a randomized 2 × 2 factorial experimental design comparing AI use and delivery mode. SETTING: The experiment was conducted online in Australia. PARTICIPANTS: The study included 710 Australian adults recruited through a paid panel. EXPOSURE: Participants were randomized to 1 of 4 hypothetical physical therapist consultation scenarios (in-person vs telerehabilitation; AI used vs not used). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Perceived warmth; competence; safety; provider trust; emotional trust; relational and functional service quality; working alliance; and intention to use were measured on 7-point Likert-scales. Composite mean scores were analyzed using ordinary least squares regression with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. RESULTS: Mean scores in the no-AI, in-person condition ranged from 4.8 to 5.8. Among in-person scenarios, described AI use was associated with lower ratings across all outcomes, including warmth (b = -0.3, 95% CI = -0.5 to -0.1), competence (-0.4, -0.6 to -0.2) and safety (-0.8, -1.1 to -0.6), provider trust (-0.5, -0.7 to -0.3) and intention to use (-0.8, -1.0 to -0.5). Without AI, telerehabilitation also reduced ratings by 0.2 to 0.7 points across outcomes. Positive interaction effects indicated attenuation of AI-related reductions in telerehabilitation for relational (interaction b = 0.4, 95% CI = 0.1 to 0.8) and functional service quality (0.36, 0.02 to 0.70), intention to use (0.6, 0.1 to 1.0), and perceived safety (0.5, 0.1 to 0.9). CONCLUSIONS: Hypothetical in-person consultations described as involving AI were associated with poorer consumer perceptions of physical therapists and services. Telerehabilitation was also perceived less favorably than in-person care. RELEVANCE: Future studies should test whether transparency and reassurance mitigate the effects of AI-use on consumer perceptions of physical therapy.

articles.title: Layered anatomy of the greater and lesser occipital nerves with photogrammetry-based three-dimensional models: a cadaveric study.
articles.authors: Wei Zhou, Haosu Zhang, Lean Sun et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The superficial neurovascular anatomy of the posterior occipital region is important for occipital nerve block, greater occipital nerve (GON) decompression, and posterior fossa incision planning. However, the continuous layered relationship between the medial GON-occipital artery (OA) region and the lateral lesser occipital nerve (LON) channel remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: This cadaveric study examined 10 formalin-fixed specimens (20 sides). Layer-by-layer dissection documented nerve courses, emergence points, diameters, terminal branches, neurovascular relationships, GON-LON communications, and relationships with the OA and adjacent muscles. Photogrammetry-based three-dimensional models were constructed for visualization, not quantitative measurement. RESULTS: The GON and LON were identified on all 20 sides. The GON had 6.0 ± 1.4 terminal branches. Its trapezius muscle/fascial emergence point was located 25.4 ± 3.2 mm horizontally from the posterior midline and 14.0 ± 2.2 mm vertically from the external occipital protuberance (EOP) level. GON-OA relationships comprised a single crossing on 3 sides, multiple crossings on 8 sides, continuous contact on 5 sides, and coiling on 4 sides. The LON traversed a trapezius muscle-related plane on 9 sides and followed a posterior sternocleidomastoid muscle-border course on 11 sides. In descriptive side-level comparisons, the trapezius muscle-related emergence point was closer to the posterior midline and EOP level but farther from the mastoid reference line than the posterior sternocleidomastoid muscle-border emergence point. GON-LON communications were observed on 17 sides. CONCLUSION: These findings support a layered, pathway-based, and conceptual zone-based model of posterior occipital neurovascular anatomy, rather than localization based only on isolated surface landmarks.

articles.title: Photobiomodulation as a contemporary antioxidant intervention in myocardial infarction.
articles.authors: Gabriel Matheus Da Silva Batista, Ighor Luiz Azevedo Teixeira, Ednei Luiz Antonio et al.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a complex cascade of structural and functional alterations that frequently culminate in adverse cardiac remodelling and heart failure. Central to this process is the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which disrupt mitochondrial function, impair calcium handling, and activate pro-apoptotic and pro-fibrotic pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has emerged as a non-invasive therapeutic approach capable of modulating several key biological processes involved in post-infarction remodelling. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate that PBM reduces infarct size, attenuates ventricular dilation, and improves both systolic and diastolic function. Through the absorption of red to near-infrared light by mitochondrial chromophores, particularly cytochrome c oxidase, PBM enhances cellular bioenergetics, modulates ROS production and activates redox-sensitive signalling pathways. These effects promote a shift from detrimental oxidative stress toward controlled ROS signalling and, in turn, facilitate cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic responses. In addition, PBM promotes the mobilization of progenitor cells, contributing to tissue repair and microvascular restoration. Although still limited, the available clinical evidence suggests that PBM may confer modest improvements in cardiac function. However, variability in treatment protocols, delivery methods and study designs currently precludes definitive conclusions regarding its clinical efficacy. In summary, PBM represents a promising strategy for modulating oxidative stress after MI, integrating metabolic, redox and signalling pathways to attenuate cardiac remodelling. Further well-designed clinical studies are required to establish standardized protocols and to clarify its therapeutic potential in cardiovascular medicine.

articles.title: A balancing act: Passive ankle exoskeletons alter neuromuscular function and postural stability during balance.
articles.authors: Jemima C N Po, James L Williamson, Jordan Yee et al.
articles.abstract: Spring-loaded passive ankle exoskeletons have the potential to modulate neuromuscular function during standing balance by altering the mechanical demands placed on the muscle-tendon units spanning the ankle joint. This study investigated the effect of exoskeleton assistance on postural stability and neuromuscular function across balance conditions of varying difficulty. We hypothesised that assistance would improve postural stability and reduce ankle plantar flexor muscle activity during balance tasks, although these benefits may vary with balance task complexity. Participants performed standing balance tasks of varying difficulty with and without rotational stiffness provided by spring-loaded ankle exoskeletons. Balance tasks included (i) quiet standing with eyes open (EO), (ii) eyes closed (EC), and (iii) reduced base of support (RBOS). We recorded centre of pressure (COP)-based postural sway measures, lower limb joint kinematics, muscle activation data from the medial (MG) and lateral gastrocnemii (LG), soleus (SOL), and tibialis anterior (TA), and MG fascicle behaviour. Exoskeleton assistance reduced LG and SOL activation but also altered joint kinematics and coordination. Ankle-based adjustments were most evident with assistance during simpler balance tasks (EO and EC), whereas assistance during the most challenging task (RBOS) was associated with increases in COP sway velocity, COP variability and TA activation. Our results suggest that despite the potential energetic benefits from offloading the plantar flexors, passive ankle exoskeletons may induce unintended effects that hinder the control of standing balance, particularly during more challenging conditions. Further work is needed to determine the mechanisms underlying these effects.

articles.title: Persistent Skeletal Deficits Following Weight Restoration in a Rodent Model of Anorexia Nervosa.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Malihe Jafari, Daniel J Brooks, Benton Swanson et al.
articles.abstract: Purpose: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is associated with significant changes in bone density and microstructure. However, the extent and nature of skeletal recovery following weight restoration is unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate these changes in bone during simulated AN in rats across short- and long-term recovery. Methods: Female Sprague Dawley rats were exposed to 50-60% food restriction for 30 days to simulate AN, followed by recovery periods of 5, 15, and 30 days. Bone parameters were assessed longitudinally using peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) and micro-computed tomography (µCT). Bodyweight and muscle strength were correlated with bone parameters. Results: AN resulted in significant reductions in total and trabecular bone density, as well as impairments in cortical and trabecular microarchitecture. Even with weight restoration, these deficits persisted and the compensatory responses were not sufficient for bone recovery. Bodyweight showed an association with total and trabecular bone density. Measures of muscle strength also correlated with total and trabecular density and were additive in multiple regression analysis prediction of total and trabecular bone density when combined with bodyweight. Conclusion: Recovery from AN-induced bone disorders is incomplete even after weight restoration and likely requires targeted interventions beyond nutritional rehabilitation. Furthermore, muscle function is an important predictor of bone health when combined with bodyweight.

articles.title: Pulsatile Perfusion Therapy Protects Internal Carotid Artery Blood Flow and Cerebrovascular Blood Oxygen Saturation with Simulated Hemorrhage in Humans.
articles.authors: Viet Q Dinh, K Austin Davis, Lindsey Peralez et al.
articles.abstract: Pulsatile Perfusion Therapy (PPT), a method we developed to induce 0.1 Hz hemodynamic oscillations (10-second cycles), protects blood oxygen saturation during ischemia. PPT via oscillatory lower body negative pressure (LBNP) protected cerebrovascular blood oxygen saturation (ScO2) during simulated hemorrhage in humans (induced via LBNP). Thigh cuff compressions are a new approach to achieve similar 0.1 Hz hemodynamic oscillations. We hypothesized that PPT via thigh cuff compressions would attenuate reductions in cerebral blood flow and cerebrovascular blood oxygen saturation during LBNP in humans. Fifteen healthy humans (6F/9M; age, 25.8 ± 4.5 y) completed two protocols of -60 mmHg LBNP. In the PPT condition, thigh cuffs intermittently inflated and deflated in 10-s cycles during the LBNP protocol. In the control condition (CON), the thigh cuffs remained deflated. Internal carotid artery (ICA) blood flow and ScO2 were measured continuously. PPT attenuated reductions in ICA blood flow (PPT: -17.6 ± 11.3% vs. CON: -31.0 ± 11.8%; P=0.02) and ScO2 (PPT: -5.2 ± 2.4% vs. CON: -7.1 ± 3.6%; P=0.07) compared to CON. These data provide evidence for PPT as a potential intervention for the treatment of cerebral hypoperfusion during hemorrhage.

articles.title: An Empirical Snapshot of Local Nutrition Governance Capacity in the Rasuwa District of Nepal Before the Flood Surge of August 2026.
articles.authors: Patrick Webb, Robin Shrestha, Shibani Ghosh
articles.abstract: On August 26, 2026, flash floods swept through the Rasuwa district of Nepal, causing mass casualties and severe destruction. Research on disasters has led to valuable recommendations on how governments can be more attentive to warning signs and react more rapidly, and how tapping into local capacity and know-how can lead to more effective responses. However, in most crises not much is known about individual or institutional capacities that predated a shock or what resources donors and governments subsequently should bolster to support emergency responses and build resilience. In this Commentary, we draw on the self-reported data of civil servants and other local professionals tasked with implementing the national multisectoral nutrition strategy in Rasuwa. Data collection in 2024 predated the flood by roughly 2 years. The survey measured routine governance capacity, not disaster-response capacity specifically, and yet such data offer some insights into local capacity before the latest disaster and help our understanding of which elements were already under strain. The aim of this Commentary is not to report full survey findings but to highlight observations most relevant to the 2026 Rasuwa flood. Broadly, we suggest that routine governance research on nutrition and other technical topics of relevance can serve as a baseline for disaster recovery and that global calls for the localization of aid require much deeper understanding and measurement of local capacity to act.

articles.title: The internal pudendal artery: a narrative review of proximal origin, accessory supply, distal branches and clinical anatomy.
articles.authors: Mugurel Constantin Rusu, Iulian Brezean
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence on the internal pudendal artery (IPA) is distributed across studies of internal iliac artery branching, accessory pudendal arteries, distal perineal branches, perforators, anastomoses and clinical applications. OBJECTIVE: To map human anatomical, imaging and surgical evidence on IPA origin, branching, accessory supply and clinically relevant variation. METHODS: This is a narrative review of the human anatomy of the internal pudendal artery. Relevant cadaveric, imaging, angiographic and surgical literature was identified through iterative database searching (PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science and Google Scholar), citation chasing, hand-searching of historical anatomical sources, and standard reference works on anatomical variation. Reports were organised by anatomical domain. Numerical findings were summarised as study-level results and crude aggregate counts; no meta-analysis was performed. RESULTS: The charted evidence base comprises 28 studies across 30 evidence-domain assignments, complemented by additional historical, female and clinical reports discussed narratively. Eleven proximal branching studies contributed 1,403 pelvic sides or halves. The crude distribution was 62.0% for a separate superior gluteal artery with a common inferior gluteal-IPA trunk, 20.0% for separate superior gluteal, inferior gluteal and pudendal arteries, 12.5% for a common superior-inferior gluteal trunk with a separate IPA, 3.2% for a three-artery common trunk, 1.4% for a common superior gluteal-IPA trunk and 0.8% unclassified. Five studies addressed accessory pudendal arteries, six addressed distal branches, perforators, morphometry or anastomoses, and eight provided clinical or contextual evidence. Accessory pudendal artery estimates varied substantially with the detection method. CONCLUSION: Read as a single arterial axis that continues beyond the pelvis into the ischioanal fossa and perineum, the IPA unifies several otherwise separate literatures - proximal branching, accessory supply, distal branches and clinical anatomy - that involve different units of analysis and detection methods. Future systematic reviews should examine proximal branching, accessory supply and selected distal outcomes separately.

articles.title: Bioerosion traces in bones reveal an increase in ethological diversity in the insect exploitation of carcasses in the late Triassic.
articles.authors: Lucca S Cunha, Francesco Battista, Heitor Francischini
articles.abstract: This study presents the first detailed description of bioerosion traces produced by insects in bones from the Santa Cruz Sequence (early Carnian, Santa Maria Supersequence, Brazil). An array of traces is reported, consisting of notches, a tube, trails of grooves attributed to the ichnotaxon Osteocallis mandibulus and ornamented depressions attributed to a new ichnotaxon Osteograptus thanatobios igen. nov. et isp. nov. The traces were likely produced by insects, but a less inclusive taxonomic attribution is currently not possible. The ethological interpretation for the bioerosion structures is that they represent feeding traces. This report increases the contrast between the Middle and Late Triassic bioerosion record, since the latter is significantly more diverse and abundant. Hypotheses related to the onset of the Carnian Humid Episode as well as taphonomic biases are discussed as possible explanations for this contrast.

articles.title: Age and ethnicity influence serum holotranscobalamin ('Active' B12) and methylmalonic acid concentrations, two markers of vitamin B12 status assessment.
articles.authors: Agata Sobczyńska-Malefora, Maheen Siddiqui, Dominic J Harrington
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Serum vitamin B12 and holotranscobalamin (holoTC) are biomarkers of vitamin B12 status, often used with confirmatory tests such as methylmalonic acid (MMA). Serum B12 concentrations vary by age and ethnicity, but the impact of these factors on holoTC is unclear. METHODS: HoloTC was measured in 61,193 samples from an ethnically-diverse hospital population in London (Jan 2022-Oct 2023). HoloTC <25, 25-70 and >70 pmol/L were classified as deficient, indeterminate and replete, respectively. MMA was measured in 12,233 patients with holoTC 25-70 pmol/L. RESULTS: HoloTC concentrations differed significantly by ethnicity. Ethnic differences were minimal in children but became apparent in adulthood, with Black patients showing the highest holoTC concentrations, Asians intermediate, and White the lowest (p < 0.001). Overall, 1.7% of patients were holoTC deficient and 25.3% indeterminate. Among patients with holoTC 25-70 pmol/L, elevated MMA occurred in 32.7% of White, 14.8% of Black and 34.1% of Asian patients (p < 0.001) using age-specific MMA cut-offs ( > 280 nmol/L for ≤65 years; >360 nmol/L for >65 years). Using a higher MMA cut-off ( > 750 nmol/L), prevalence fell to 4.0%, 1.2%, and 4.7%, respectively. The overall prevalence of vitamin B12 deficiency in the entire cohort was 7.8% or 2.4%, depending on the MMA threshold. Compared with White patients, Black patients were 34.6% less likely to have elevated MMA. CONCLUSIONS: HoloTC and MMA concentrations vary significantly by age and ethnicity. Black adults exhibited higher holoTC and lower MMA concentrations, suggesting better B12 status or differences in metabolism. Age- and ethnicity-specific reference ranges for holoTC and MMA should be considered.

articles.title: Determining the association between gender-related factors and the perception of exertional dyspnoea in healthy males and females.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Jasvir K Dhaliwal, Jack R Dunsford, Gracie O Grift et al.
articles.abstract: The perception exertional dyspnoea is greater in females than males at absolute, but not relative, levels of minute ventilation (VE). The mechanisms of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea are unclear, but since dyspnoea perception is influenced by psychological, social, and cultural factors, it is possible that gender-related characteristics confound the assessment of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea. We sought to determine the association between gender-related characteristics and dyspnoea during exercise in males and females. Forty-six healthy adults (n=22 males, n=24 females) completed the Stanford Gender-related Variables for Health Research questionnaire to assess their gender-related characteristics (i.e., caregiver strain, work strain, independence, risk-taking, emotional intelligence, social support, and discrimination), spirometry, and an incremental cycle exercise test. Throughout exercise, standard cardiorespiratory parameters were monitored, and dyspnoea perception was assessed using the Borg scale. Females had significantly higher scores than males for emotional intelligence (p=0.029) and social support (p=0.049); whereas other gender-related characteristics were similar between the sexes (all p>0.05). Females reported significantly higher dyspnoea intensity and unpleasantness ratings than males at a V̇E of 80 l·min-1 (both p<0.05); however, males had higher dyspnoea intensity ratings at 20 and 40 % of maximum voluntary ventilation (MVV; both p<0.05). After adjusting for sex, height, body mass, and age, emotional intelligence was significantly associated with dyspnoea intensity at a V̇E of 50 l·min-1 and 50 %MVV (R2=0.14-0.18, all p<0.05). Our findings suggest that gender-related characteristics influence the perception of exertional dyspnoea, and may confound the assessment of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea perception.

articles.title: Effect of ageing on human skeletal muscle nitrate and nitrite metabolism.
articles.authors: Raghini Rajaram, Matthew I Black, Chenguang Wei et al.
articles.abstract: Ageing-associated impairment in cardiovascular function is hallmarked by decreased endogenous nitric oxide (NO) production via NO synthase (NOS) activity. Nitrate (NO3 -) in mammalian skeletal muscle may provide a substrate for an alternative NO3 --nitrite (NO2 -)-NO pathway. Here, we report the effect of ageing on NO3 - storage and metabolism in human skeletal muscle. We evaluated skeletal muscle [NO3 -] and [NO2 -], and the mRNA and protein expression of NO3 - and NO2 - transporting (sialin, CLC1) and reducing (XOR) proteins in young and older humans. Nineteen young (18-30 years) and 19 older (60-80 years) healthy adults provided blood and muscle samples without ingestion of dietary NO3 - (CON) and 3 h after a bolus ingestion of dietary NO3 -. Compared with young adults, the skeletal muscle of older adults had greater [NO3 -] (86.9 ± 38.2 vs. 64.3 ± 23.1 nmol g-1, P = 0.0334) and [NO2 -] (1.2 ± 0.4 vs. 0.8 ± 0.2 nmol g-1, P < 0.001) under the CON condition, and greater [NO3 -] (156.5 ± 50.6 vs. 122.7 ± 38.1 nmol g-1, P = 0.0258) but not [NO2 -] (1.3 ± 0.4 vs. 1.3 ± 0.6 nmol g-1, P = 0.808) post-NO3 - ingestion. The expression of sialin, CLC1 and XOR proteins was not different between age groups although there was evidence of deficiencies in the translation efficiency and protein stability of XOR, post-NO3 - ingestion, in the older adults. Muscle NO3 - uptake was unaffected by age, and older adults had equivalent or better NO3 - to NO2 - reduction efficiency compared with young adults. These results suggest that the NO3 --NO2 --NO pathway may mitigate lowered NO production from the NOS pathway in healthy older adults. KEY POINTS: Nitrate (NO3 -) in mammalian skeletal muscle may provide a substrate for the NO3 --nitrite (NO2 -)-nitric oxide (NO) pathway when endogenous NO production via NO synthase (NOS) activity is adversely affected by age. We show that skeletal muscle of older adults has greater baseline [NO3 -] and [NO2 -], as well as a greater [NO3 -] following bolus dietary NO3 - ingestion, compared with young adults. The expression of NO3 - transporting and reducing proteins was unaffected by age, but the translation efficiency of xanthine oxidoreductase was reduced post-NO3 - ingestion in older adults. Muscle NO3 - uptake was unaffected by age, and older adults had equivalent or better capacity for NO3 - to NO2 - reduction compared with young adults. The NO3 --NO2 --NO pathway has the potential to mitigate lowered NO production from the NOS pathway in healthy older adults.

articles.title: Surgical anatomy of the hypoglossal canal - systematic review with meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Daniel Gondorf, George Triantafyllou, Panagiotis Papadopoulos-Manolarakis et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The hypoglossal canal (HC) is a vital conduit for the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) and venous structures. Variations in its morphology, particularly bony septations, can complicate skull-base surgeries such as transcondylar or far-lateral approaches. This study aims to provide a meta-analysis of HC prevalence, morphometry, and surgical landmarks. MATERIALS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted through December 2025 following PRISMA guidelines. Pooled prevalence and mean dimensions were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses explored the impact of sex, side, nationality, and study type. Leave-one-out analysis was performed to evaluate the source of heterogeneity. RESULTS: Thirty-three studies involving 10,132 skulls were included. The pooled prevalence of a typical (non-septated) HC was 60.39% (95% CI: 46.67-73.34). Variations occurred in nearly 40% of cases, including incomplete (18.85%) and complete (17.74%) septations. A significant discrepancy was found between study types: cadaveric studies reported a complete septation prevalence of 35.39%, while imaging studies detected only 9.03% (p = 0.0070). Morphometric analysis established the HC is located within a mean distance of 10.0-10.8 mm (95% CI: 9.12-12.11) from the posterior and anterior margins of the occipital condyle. No significant differences were observed based on sex or laterality. Substantial heterogeneity and potential publication bias through asymmetry test was detected. CONCLUSIONS: Structural variations of the HC are frequent developmental variants rather than rare anomalies. The significant under-detection of septations by imaging suggests that standard preoperative CT may overlook complex neural or venous partitioning. A 10 mm distance from the condylar margins may serve as a practical anatomical reference for individual preoperative assessment to avoid iatrogenic injury to CN XII during condylar drilling.

articles.title: Rare association of metoptic canal and Warwick's foramen in an adult skull - anatomical case report and embryological considerations.
articles.authors: Cezar Octavian Morosanu, Amy Manson, Alistair P Bond
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accessory foramina of the orbital apex are anatomical variants with potential radiological and surgical implications. Although individually uncommon, the simultaneous presence of multiple accessory foramina within the same orbit has rarely been reported. METHODS: During a routine osteological examination, a rare association of Warwick's foramen (WF) and metoptic canal (MC) was identified in the right orbit of an adult skull. Morphometric assessment was undertaken, and a review of current literature was also performed to investigate the characteristics of these variants. RESULTS: WF measured 2.94 (± 0.38) mm × 1.94 (± 0.33) mm, with a canal length of 1.03 (± 0.09) mm, whereas the MC measured 0.73 (± 0.18) mm in diameter and 2.28 (± 0.79) mm in length. Their distances from the optic canal were 8.55 ± 0.29 and 1.07 ± 0.18 mm, respectively. CONCLUSION: This case documents the rare ipsilateral association of WF and MC in the same orbital apex, highlighting the complexity of this region. Recognising these structures is important in radiological assessment, as well as in pre- and intraoperative settings.

articles.title: Morphologic characterisation and anatomical variations of superior cerebellar artery in Indian angiographic cohort.
articles.authors: Vinod Singh Jatav, Abdul Muqueet Shaikh, Sneh Jain et al.
articles.abstract: AIMS: To identify and evaluate the morphological and anatomical variations of the superior cerebellar arteries by using Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA). MATERIAL AND METHODS: A total of 105 patients (67 males and 38 females) who underwent cerebral DSA included in this retrospective descriptive observational study (from 1st September 2024 to 31 October 2025). Angiograms were reviewed for morphological characteristics and anatomical variations of the superior cerebellar arteries. RESULTS: A total of 105 patients (67 males and 38 females), comprising 253 SCAs, were studied. Out of the 105 patients, 33 (31.4%) had duplicated SCAs, which were more common on the left side (14.3%). Of the 253 SCAs, 159 (62.8%) originated from the basilar artery, 13 (5.14%) from the P1 segment of the PCA and 81 (32%) had common SCA-PCA origin. Symmetrical SCA origin was observed in 77 (73.3%) of the 105 patients, whereas 28 (26.67%) patients had asymmetrical SCA origins. The mean diameter of the first segment of the SCA was 1.00 mm on the left side (95% CI 0.96-1.04 mm) and 1.01 mm on the right side (95% CI 0.97-1.05 mm). The mean length of the first segment of the SCA was 15.56 mm on the left side (95% CI 14.96-16.16 mm) and 16.57 mm (95% CI 15.86-17.08 mm) on the right side. Early bifurcation was observed in 43 patients (40.95%) with 12 on the left side (11.4%) and 23 SCAs (21.9%) on the right side. Interrater reliability demonstrated moderate to excellent agreement for categorical and continuous variables, with Cohen's κ ranging from 0.353 to 1.000 and ICC values ranging from 0.679 to 1.000. CONCLUSION: In this angiographic series, duplicated SCA and SCA-PCA common trunk origin were relatively frequent. Recognition of these variations enhance the safety of neuro-interventional technique and approach for micro neurosurgical procedures involving the posterior circulation.

articles.title: Ultra-processed foods intake and risk of Helicobacter pylori infection: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Kexin Li, Ziyuan Ma, Juanjuan Liu et al.
articles.abstract: Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) are closely associated with gut microbiota diversity and functionality. The gut microbiota plays a role in developing Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection. However, no cohort studies have explored the association between UPFs intake and the risk of H. pylori infection in the general population. In total, 1,769 participants without baseline H. pylori infection were enrolled in this study from the TCLSIH Cohort Study. Information on UPFs intake was obtained from a validated food frequency questionnaire, and H. pylori infection was diagnosed by using the 13C-urea breath test. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models adjusted for potential confounding factors were used to examine the association between UPFs intake and the risk of H. pylori infection. During a median follow-up of 2.0 years, the incidence rate of H. pylori infection was 20.92%. The multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HR; 95% confidence intervals) of H. pylori infection across increasing quartiles of UPFs intake were 1.00 (reference), 1.12 (0.79, 1.58), 0.84 (0.57, 1.23) and 0.86 (0.57, 1.29) (P for trend = 0.24) in males, and 1.00 (reference), 1.41 (0.74, 2.69), 1.49 (0.77, 2.88) and 2.72 (1.39, 5.33) (P for trend < 0.01) in females, respectively. This study shows that higher UPFs intake is associated with a higher risk of H. pylori infection in females, while no association was found in males. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Cranial and endocranial anatomy of Gregorymys mixtecorum (Rodentia, Geomyidae) and the interpretation of its ecomorph.
articles.authors: Paulina Moctezuma-Duclaud, Jair Israel Barrientos-Lara, Jesús Alvarado-Ortega
articles.abstract: The relationship between neuroanatomical shape and ecomorphology remains a topic of debate in mammalian evolutionary biology. While previous studies on sciurids suggested that brain endocasts could reliably reflect locomotor habits, this correlation has not been extensively tested across broader rodent lineages. This study describes the neuroanatomy of the extinct geomyid Gregorymys mixtecorum for the first time, in order to evaluate whether its endocranial morphology allows interpretation of locomotor ecomorphology in the absence of postcranial elements. Using high-resolution computed tomography, we reconstructed the brain endocasts of two new G. mixtecorum specimens alongside 19 newly scanned extant rodent species. These data were integrated with a previously published landmark-based sciurid dataset to perform Geometric Morphometric analyses, including Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Procrustes ANOVA. Our results reveal that PC1 and PC2 account for 18.78% and 16.82% of the variance, respectively. Crucially, Procrustes ANOVA demonstrates that while ecomorphology explains 24.15% of the morphological variation, taxonomic family accounts for a significantly higher proportion (48.87%). These findings indicate that rodent endocast shape is primarily constrained by phylogenetic history. However, the significant ecological signal (24.15%) suggests that locomotor adaptations exert a distinct selective pressure on neuroanatomy. Rather than producing identical gross morphologies across disparate clades, which is prevented by deep phylogenetic constraints, ecological factors may drive parallel morphological shifts within independent lineages. Consequently, while the general endocast shape is heavily driven by evolutionary history, localized anatomical structures can still serve as reliable predictors for inferring ecomorphology in extinct geomyids, as long as evolutionary variations unique to each lineage are considered as a baseline.

articles.title: Interaction between 3-SNP genetic risk score and lifestyle risk score on cardiovascular risk factors and the risk of lifetime ASCVD among overweight and obese women.
articles.authors: Sahand Tehrani Fateh, Farideh Shiraseb, Viviane Z Rocha et al.
articles.abstract: Interaction between genetic variations and lifestyle risk factors has been shown to be associated with atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD). This study for the first time sought to investigate this interaction on cardiovascular risk factors and the lifetime ASCVD risk in Iranian obese and overweight women. This study consisted of 256 overweight or obese women. The genetic risk score (GRS) included three genetic variations (CAV-1 rs3807992, CRY-1 rs2287161 and MC4R rs17782313), and each of them was genotyped using PCR-restriction fragment length polymorphism. Lifestyle risk score (LRS) consisting of dietary behaviour, physical activity, sleep quality, socio-economic status and waist-to-stature ratio was used to assess lifestyle risk factors associated with ASCVD, and the Bonferroni correction was also applied for multiple comparisons. Following Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons using a family-wise approach (α = 0·0028 for interaction analyses), the interaction between high LRS and high GRS was not significantly associated with any assessed cardiovascular risk factor or lifetime ASCVD risk. The nominal P-values for these interactions were 0·040 (CRI-II), 0·038 (CHOLINDEX), 0·018 (TyG-BMI), 0·041 (TAG), 0·041 (AIP), 0·067 (HDL), 0·075 (LDL) and 0·077 (ASCVD lifetime risk), all of which exceeded the Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold. In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating study, uncorrected analyses suggested preliminary nominally significant interactions. However, after adjusting for multiple comparisons, no definitive evidence of GRS × LRS interactions was observed. These findings require replication in larger, prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Qualitative and quantitative characterisation of smooth muscle in the human ​common bile duct.
articles.authors: Aryan K Sharma, Jaimin P Chauhan, Abed M Zaitoun et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The distribution and abundance of smooth muscle within the human common bile duct (CBD) remain incompletely characterised, with previous studies relying predominantly on qualitative assessment. This study aimed to characterise smooth-muscle architecture within the human ​CBD using complementary qualitative assessment and semi-automated quantitative digital image analysis. METHODS: ​CBD specimens from 106 pancreaticoduodenectomies and 3 total pancreatectomies were stained for desmin, smooth muscle actin (SMA) and calretinin and analysed using QuPath ( https://qupath.github.io ). RESULTS: Desmin-positive smooth muscle was identified in all specimens and was predominantly scattered (44.0%) or interrupted (26.6%), while focal (25.7%) and continuous circumferential (3.7%) patterns were less frequent. Median desmin-positive area was 1.86% (IQR 1.17-2.79%), compared with 33.55% (IQR 25.96-43.54%) for SMA. Qualitative desmin classification demonstrated moderate concordance with quantitative desmin-positive area (ρ = 0.515, p < 0.001). Smooth-muscle abundance and distribution did not differ significantly between malignant and non-malignant specimens and were not associated with preoperative bilirubin or CBD wall thickness. Malignant specimens demonstrated greater CBD wall thickness than non-malignant specimens despite similar smooth-muscle abundance. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that smooth muscle is consistently identifiable but predominantly sparse and discontinuously distributed within the surgically resected human ​CBD. Semi-automated digital image analysis provides an objective approach to its quantification; however, studies incorporating disease-free controls and functional assessment are required to determine the physiological significance of these findings.

articles.title: Morphology of the endocranial cavities of Stratiotosuchus maxhechti (Notosuchia, Mesoeucrocodylia) from the Late Cretaceous of Brazil.
articles.authors: Philippe George Azambuja, Paulo Victor Luiz Gomes da Costa Pereira, Athirson de Souza Albuquerque et al.
articles.abstract: Notosuchia is a group of mostly terrestrial crocodylomorphs found predominantly in the Mesozoic of Gondwana. Currently, approximately 30 specimens have been reported from the Bauru Group (Paraná Basin) in southeastern Brazil. Baurusuchidae, a notosuchian group comprising only terrestrial species, is typically recovered from the Late Cretaceous of the Bauru Group and includes Stratiotosuchus maxhechti, the focus of this study. Here, we focus on the holotype, recovered from an outcrop of the Adamantina Formation (Paraná Basin) in São Paulo State. The specimen was subjected to computed tomography (CT) to study its encephalic endocast, paratympanic sinus system, nasal cavities, and associated structures. One of these associated structures, the paranasal sinus system, is similar to those described in the literature for other notosuchians, such as Campinasuchus and Barreirosuchus, with pneumatic structures within the maxilla and jugal, as well as a lacrimal sinus. The olfactory region was present, with a morphology different from that of extant taxa (e.g., dorsoventral flattening of the structure) and more similar to the patterns described for other oreinirostral skulls. Despite the poor preservation of the encephalic endocast, it was possible to identify morphological patterns consistent with those reported in other baurusuchids, namely a sigmoid-shaped encephalon oriented almost horizontally, distinct from that of the extant crocodyliform described herein. The paratympanic sinuses were much more complex than in extant taxa. This structure shows high plasticity within the crocodyliform lineage, probably representing a basal characteristic associated with terrestrial habits that was lost in several lineages, especially in aquatic and semiaquatic forms. The paratympanic sinuses and the development of the olfactory region are possible indicators of the importance of sensory organs in supporting the hypercarnivorous paleoecological role historically interpreted for this taxon in the Late Cretaceous of the Bauru Group.

articles.title: Protection by ascorbate and catechin at high physiological concentrations against myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in an isolated rat heart model.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Ahmed Abou Hadeed, Kosar Omidian, Hossein Rafiei et al.
articles.abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is an important health concern in myocardial infarction and situations such as angioplasty and cardiac surgeries. Ascorbate (vitamin C) and flavonoids such as catechin are known for their antioxidant activity and are of interest as supplements or added to perfused blood during surgeries to limit I/R injury. While intravenous ascorbate during surgeries has been studied in clinical trials, it has usually been at high pharmacological concentrations (with potential unwanted prooxidant activity). The objectives of this study were to 1) determine the extent to which ascorbate or catechin alone, added to the perfusate at levels which could be in blood after dietary supplementation, can protect myocardial tissue in the reperfusion phase of I/R injury, and 2) evaluate the possible cooperative or synergistic protective effect of ascorbate and catechin when given together.
